JUDGMENT MFA No.25266/2012 is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.261/2011 dated 22.05.2012 passed by Addl. Senior Civil Judge and AMACT., Haveri.

entities.text: Addl. Senior Civil Judge and AMACT., Haveri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.20844/2012 is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.18/2011 dated 24.09.2011, by Fast Track Court and MACT., Haveri.
3. MFA No.24041/2012 is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.261/2011 by the Addl. Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Haveri for enhancement of compensation.

4. In both the claim petitions, it is stated that on 30.06.2009 at 8.15 p.m. on Haveri-Hangal road near fire station at Haveri, claimant Veeresh in MVC No.261/2011 along with one Basavaraju was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 and at that time another motorcycle bearing No.KA-30/E-2701 coming from NC: 2023:KHC-D:8972 C/W MFA No. 20844 of 2012, opposite direction and both the vehicles have been dashed each other resulting into the injuries to the rider Veeresh of motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 had sustained injuries and the deceased Mehaboob Ali rider of vehicle bearing No.KA-30/E-2701 died in the accident.
5. The rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 Veeresh, has filed claim petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act,1988 for seeking compensation.

The legal heirs of Mehaboob Ali have filed claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act contending that Veeresh who is rider of the motorcycle No.KA-47/E-1419 was rash and negligent and caused accident, resulting to the death of Mehaboob Ali.

6. The learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that the claim petition filed in MVC No.261/2011 by Veeresh under Section 163-A of MV Act is not maintainable for the reason that the said rider entered into the shoes of the owner of the motorcycle.

Therefore, the claim petition filed under Section 163-A is not NC: 2023:KHC-D:8972 C/W MFA No. 20844 of 2012, maintainable and he places reliance on the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramkhiladi and another Vs. United India Insurance Company and another1.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi and another Vs. United India Insurance Company and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Further, it is submitted that in the claim petition in MVC No.18/2011, the rider of the offending motorcycle namely Veeresh was not holding driving license and the owner of the motorcycle has not produced the driving license inspite of notice issued to him.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419.
8. In the present cases, the claimant was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 dashed the motorcycle bearing No.KA-30/E-2701.

The claimant filed petition under Section 163-A of MV The Manager National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Prakash Channabasappa Angadi on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124635635/
4 Act, 1988. The AIR 2020 SC 527 NC: 2023:KHC-D:8972 C/W MFA No. 20844 of 2012, respondent No.1-Prakash is the owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant Veeresh entered into the shoes of the owner of the said motorcycle and filed claim petition.
Therefore, the issue involved is no more res-integra in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramkhiladi(supra).
Therefore, the claimant Veeresh cannot maintain claim petition under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, as he has entered shoes of the owner of the motorcycle.
Therefore, the Tribunal has erred in entertaining the claim petition and awarding the compensation.
Therefore, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the insurance company is allowed.
Consequently, when the judgment and award passed in MVC No.261/2011 filed by rider- Veeresh is liable to be set aside, hence, there is no question of enhancement of compensation.
Resultantly appeal in MVC No.24041/2012 filed for enhancement of compensation is dismissed.

In the present case, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the insurance company that the driver of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 was not holding driving license to drive the motorcycle.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner and to pay compensation.
Therefore, prays for absolving the liability to pay the compensation.
10. In this case, the owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 has entered into appearance but has not produced driving license.
The Insurance Company has issued notice to the owner of the said motorcycle for production of driving license and other particulars and records.
But, the owner has not produced driving license.
Exs. R2
and R3
are the registered notice issued by the insurance company and the acknowledgment which proves that the owner has received the notice issued by the insurance company.

But, the owner even after receipt of NC: 2023:KHC-D:8972 C/W MFA No.
20844 of 2012, the notice has not produced driving license either to the insurance company or to the tribunal.

Even, the owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/E-1419 is having an opportunity to produce driving license before this Court in this appeal, by way of an additional evidence to produce driving license but that is not produced.
Therefore, there is evidence that the claimant Veeresh was not having driving license to drive the motorcycle.
Hence, there is a breach of conditions of insurance policy.
Therefore, the insurance company is liable to be absolved from indemnifying the owner of the motorcycle.

11. However, as per Sub-section (2) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, when the Insurance Company established the fact that driver was not holding driving license, then as per Sub-sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company as if the judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in respect of third parties and then recover the same from owner of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, order of pay and recovery - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:8972 C/W MFA No. 20844 of 2012, is made as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pappu and others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and The Manager National Insurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur vs. Yallavva w/o. Yamanappa Dharanakeri3 12.

To this extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

13. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.25266/2012 filed by the insurance company is allowed.
